machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:ו: In Milchamot part 3—on the above doubt whether women in birkat hamazon are obligated from the Torah.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.8:א: (s.k. 8) And deaf, etc.—see siman 55 seif 8—for prayer the law is so; and the same for zimun.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.8:ב: And in responsum of Maharil, etc.—meaning Levush was forced to settle Rama's language; and to Magen Avraham it appears from Rama's stam and also in Likutei Maharil—from where Rama's law flows—he also wrote stam deaf and fool; and it is forced that he intended specifically deaf-mute who speaks, etc.; and fool who is not a complete fool—but the disciple who wrote Likutei Maharil erred in Maharil's intent; and always the disciple's view in Likutei Maharil is even complete deaf and fool combine—for he understood what Maharil wrote in responsum to one who says a minor, etc.—so too deaf, etc.; but we do not hold thus. And it was Rama's view to the disciple that what he wrote and we do not hold thus refers specifically to minor lying in a cradle; but deaf and fool—even for us he combines—for he is better than minor of Mishna Berurah. And this is Maharil's intent: since there is an opinion that even minor of Mishna Berurah combines—even though we do not hold thus—nevertheless so too deaf and fool for us in any case combine; and similarly Maharil wrote regarding prayer: if one of ten sleeps—nevertheless he combines—for there is an opinion that even minor of Mishna Berurah combines; and even though we do not hold like him—nevertheless for sleeping who is better—even for us he combines—they brought Magen Avraham above siman 55 s.k. 8 see there; but in truth this is not Maharil's intent—that deaf and fool are not better than minor of Mishna Berurah; and as for us minor of Mishna Berurah does not combine—so too deaf and fool; and Maharil did not write deaf and fool combine except per one who says minor of Mishna Berurah combines; and what Maharil concluded and we do not hold thus refers both to minor and to deaf and fool.

magen-avraham/part-001.txt.3:_: Am ha'aretz complete—for in the Gemara they say that even if he read and learned and did not serve Torah scholars to understand reasons of mishnayot to ask and answer—they do not invite zimun on him; and therefore he said that even am ha'aretz complete they invite zimun on him in this time—for if they separated from them they would also separate from the congregation entirely; and if he does not recite Keriat Shema they do not invite zimun on him (Shach); and per R' Yitzchak's reason they invite zimun on every am ha'aretz (Kenesset HaGedolah); and in my humble opinion it is not applicable that each build a bamah for himself—since most am ha'aretz recite Keriat Shema; and for an individual we do not care.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.4:_: And did not immerse—and whenever he did not immerse properly he is called did not immerse, as written in Yoreh Deah siman 124 seif 2; and it is obvious that one wicked publicly transgressing sins—and all the more a mumar—they do not invite zimun on him, for he is no worse than am ha'aretz in Talmudic times.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.5:_: Exempt from blessing—meaning whenever his dead lies before him; see siman 71.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.6:_: Because of promiscuity of slaves—and therefore even if there are three slaves they do not invite zimun with women in one company; but with others they invite zimun when there are three without the women; as written seif 7.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.7:_: Even though they do not understand—and nevertheless they must understand birkat hamazon, as written siman 193 (Levush); and Levush wrote most women understand somewhat; and see there.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.10:א: The toddlers—about nine or ten years old; and specifically one and not two, whether for three or ten (Shach); see siman 55 seif 4—for in prayer he does not combine since he cannot exempt himself from it—not so birkat hamazon—for if he wants he need not eat (Terumat HaDeshen).
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.10:ב: We establish him as an adult—meaning one need not check for two hairs; but if we know he did not bring two hairs they do not invite zimun on him, as written siman 55 seif 5; and if he brought two hairs before thirteen it does not help; and it appears to me specifically for combination; but to discharge others we require we know certainly he brought two hairs through examination or his beard filled in, as written Choshen Mishpat siman 35—for behold birkat hamazon is also d'oraisa and we do not rely on presumption; and in Yeshuot Yaakov chapter 7 of Bava Kamma 37 he wrote that from the Torah an adult fulfills through blessing of the minor—only the Sages forbade; therefore they rely on presumption—until here; and it requires study—for in siman 186 seif 8 it implies it is d'oraisa since they ruled the doubt stringently; and further in seif 2 it says that one a son blesses, etc.; and so in Gemara Berachot daf 20; and it is difficult to answer—for since he does not know to bless the Sages did not decree lest he be idle from birkat hamazon d'oraisa, as written siman 193; and further the main reason we hold even though he fulfills he discharges—is because all Israel are guarantors for one another as stated end of chapter 3 of Rosh Hashanah; and for a minor arevut is not applicable; and from the Torah he is completely exempt—how can the adult discharge; therefore it appears what he wrote is primary; and see Beit Yosef; and afterward I found he wrote in Milchamot part 3 of Berachot explicitly it is d'oraisa—see there; however if each blesses for himself we do not care; see end of siman 186.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.10:ג: And deaf—specifically deaf-mute who speaks and does not hear; and fool who is not a complete fool; see siman 55 seif 8 (Levush); and in responsum Maharil siman 224 he wrote: per one who says minor lying in cradle combines for ten—so too deaf and fool who ate where the Shechinah rests; but we do not hold thus—until here; perhaps the disciple heard and erred and thought that for everyone the law is so; see siman 55 seif 6.

mechaber/part-001.txt.1:main: On whom one invites zimun and on whom one does not. It contains 11 seifim: The waiter who ate a kezayit—they invite zimun on him.
mechaber/part-001.txt.2:main: A Cuthean nowadays is like an idolater and they do not invite zimun on him.
mechaber/part-001.txt.3:main: Am ha'aretz complete—they invite zimun on him in this time.
mechaber/part-001.txt.4:main: A gentile—they do not invite zimun on him. Even a convert who was circumcised and did not immerse—they do not invite zimun on him. But a complete convert—they invite zimun on him; and he may bless birkat hamazon and say al shehinchalta to our forefathers.
mechaber/part-001.txt.5:main: An onen on a weekday who is exempt from blessing—they do not invite zimun on him.
mechaber/part-001.txt.6:main: Women, slaves, and minors—they do not invite zimun on them; but they invite zimun among themselves. A company of women, slaves, and minors should not invite zimun together because of promiscuity of slaves; rather women among themselves and slaves among themselves—provided they do not invite zimun with the Name.
mechaber/part-001.txt.7:main: Women invite zimun among themselves—reshut; but when they eat with men they are obligated and fulfill through our zimun. {Rama: Even though they do not understand (Rosh and Mordechai beginning of chapter three who ate, in the name of Rashi).}
mechaber/part-001.txt.8:main: An androgynous invites zimun with his kind; and he does not invite zimun neither with men nor with women.
mechaber/part-001.txt.9:main: A tumtum does not invite zimun at all.
mechaber/part-001.txt.10:main: A minor who reached the season of toddlers and knows to whom they bless—they invite zimun on him and he combines whether for three or ten. {Rama: And some say they do not combine him at all until he is thirteen years old—for then we establish him as an adult who brought two hairs (Rosh and Mordechai chapter three who ate, and Tur); and so is the practice and one should not deviate. And deaf and fool—if they have intent and understanding they combine for zimun even though the deaf one does not hear the berachah (Maharil).}
mechaber/part-001.txt.11:main: One whom they excommunicated for a sin—they do not invite zimun on him.

mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:_: (1) They invite zimun on him—for even though he did not fix himself at the table with them—that he eats standing and also goes and comes in the middle of his eating and has no fixity at all with them—nevertheless he combines, since his way of eating is thus—this is his fixity; not so another person, as written in siman 197 seif 2 in Mishna Berurah.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.3:_: (2) Am ha'aretz complete—for in the Gemara they say that even if he read and learned and did not serve Torah scholars—that is, to understand reasons of mishnayot to ask and answer—they do not invite zimun on him; and therefore he said that even am ha'aretz complete who has no mikra and mishnah—they invite zimun on him in this time—for if they separated from them they would also separate from the congregation entirely; and if he does not fulfill mitzvot of the Torah in a matter publicized among all Israel—such as he does not recite Keriat Shema morning and evening—some say even so they invite zimun on him; and Magen Avraham's view is that in this they do not invite zimun on him—for here since all Israel recite Keriat Shema we are not concerned for damage in what we separate ourselves from individuals who do not recite; and so concluded several Acharonim; and all the more one wicked transgressing sins publicly—they do not invite zimun on him [Magen Avraham and Shulchan Aruch HaRav].
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.4:א: (3) Idolater—not, etc.—meaning even if he intended to bless the God of Israel.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.4:ב: (4) And did not immerse—and whenever he did not immerse as the law before a court of three as explained in Yoreh Deah siman 268 seif 1—he is called did not immerse [Acharonim].
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.4:ג: (5) They do not invite zimun on him—for he is not a convert until he circumcises and immerses.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.4:ד: (6) And he may bless—and meaning even to discharge others their obligation in birkat hamazon [Beit Yosef].
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.4:ה: (7) To our forefathers—for to Abraham the land was given as inheritance and Abraham was called father of a multitude of nations.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.5:א: (8) Who is exempt from blessing—meaning whenever his dead lies before him, as in siman 71.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.5:ב: (9) They do not invite zimun—and even per those who say if he wanted to be stringent and answer and bless the permission is in his hand—nevertheless since he is exempt he does not combine; and see what we wrote above in siman 71 s.k. 4 in Mishna Berurah regarding if there is a company in the city designated for escorting the dead and they handed him over to them.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.5:ג: (10) On him—and even b'dieved if he blessed to discharge others it does not help—for whoever is himself exempt from the matter cannot discharge others [Peri Megadim].
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.6:ב: (12) They do not invite zimun on them—meaning if there were only two men—these do not combine to three to become obligated through them in zimun—for they are not subject to obligation in zimun, as below in seif 7; and even if they wanted to invite zimun with them—they are also not permitted; and they are worse than women by themselves or slaves who have at least permission to invite zimun, as below—because their company is not fitting that combination of three be through women; and similarly through slaves who are promiscuous in licentiousness; and even a woman with her husband and sons—it is also not proper to combine for this reason.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.6:ג: (13) But they invite zimun among themselves—reshut; and it refers to men and slaves, not minors—for minors are not subject to mitzvah to say they invite among themselves.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.6:ד: (14) Promiscuity of slaves—for they are suspected of licentiousness and homosexuality; therefore even if there are three slaves they do not invite zimun with women in one company—for there is still promiscuity.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.6:ה: (15) With the Name—for mention of the Name is a holy matter; and every holy matter is not with fewer than ten free males, as above in siman 55.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:א: (23) Who reached, etc.—and less than this his da'at is not considered at all—even if he knows to whom they bless.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:ב: (24) The toddlers—meaning about nine or ten [Magen Avraham]; and some say the same below this measure if he is only from six years and up—if he is sharp and knows to whom they bless.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:ג: (25) And he combines, etc.—meaning one and not two, whether for three or ten.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:ד: (26) Whether for three, etc.—and that which is stated in seif 6 they do not invite zimun on minors—it deals with very young minors or one who does not know to whom they bless.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:ה: (27) For then we establish him, etc.—for we say once he reached the category of years—presumably he already brought two hairs and one need not check afterward; but if they checked him and found he has no two hairs—we do not combine him for zimun. And all these views are only for combination that he combine for three and ten; but that he be the inviter and discharge others in birkat hamazon—for everyone he does not discharge until he is thirteen years and one day and known that he brought two hairs—for birkat hamazon is from the Torah and for Torah matters we do not rely on this presumption that presumably he brought; however if the inviter says only n'varech and each in birkat hamazon blesses alone for himself as our custom [as explained in siman 183 seif 7]—we do not care—for since he is thirteen years we rely on presumption for this.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:ו: (28) And deaf—it deals with deaf-mute who speaks and does not hear—for in complete deaf we hold he is exempt from all mitzvot like a minor who lacks da'at, as above siman 55 seif 8, and he does not combine. And deaf who hears and does not speak—see in Peri Megadim.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.10:ז: (29) And fool—not dealing with complete fool—for this one does not combine; but one who is not so wise as other people and the public hold him as a fool.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.11:_: (30) They do not invite zimun on him—whether for three or ten—for this is language of excommunication that they distance and separate him from their group; and see above in siman 55 seif 12 in Biur Halacha.
